text: Once upon a time, a mother pig lived with her three little pigs.
"You're all grown up now. Go and build your own homes!"
The oldest pig found a sunny meadow.
What do you think he built his house with?
That's okay! Let's pick something from the meadow.
Wow, an ice cream house! But it melted in the warm sun.
Let's try something else. What should he use?
Paper! The oldest pig folded, and folded, and folded.
Straw! The oldest pig tied bundle after bundle.
His paper house was finished! He felt very proud.
His straw house was finished! He felt very proud.
Then along came a hungry wolf. "Whoo… whoo…"
He blew and he blew. What happened to the house?
That's right! The light paper house blew away.
That's right! The light straw house blew away.
The oldest pig ran to his brother's house.
The oldest pig hoped so too. But the paper house was too light, and it blew away.
The oldest pig hoped so too. But the straw house was too light, and it blew away.
The middle pig was building at the edge of the forest.
Yum! But the ants came and ate it all up.
Let's use something the forest has lots of.
Wood! The middle pig stacked log after log.
It looked much stronger than the paper house!
It looked much stronger than the straw house!
But the wolf came back. "Whoo… whoo… CRASH!"
The wood house tumbled down! The little pigs hurried away together.
The youngest pig said, "This time, let's build a house the wolf can never blow down!"
What should he build it with?
Great idea! Let's use bricks. They're hard, just like stones!
Hmm, remember the paper house? It blew away.
Hmm, remember the straw house? It blew away.
What is heavy and strong?
Let's think together! Should it be heavy, or light?
Feathers would fly away with one puff! Let's try something heavy.
Bricks! The youngest pig stacked them one by one.
The wolf blew until his cheeks turned red. "WHOOOO!"
But the brick house didn't move one bit! Why do you think it stayed?
That's right! The heavy, strong brick house stood up to the wind.
The wolf scratched his head and wandered away.
And the three little pigs danced in front of their brick house. The End!
Good night, little one. It's time to close your eyes.
The moon peeked over the hill and smiled at the sleepy town.
"Who's there?" whispered the little rabbit.
Once upon a time, a tiny dragon was afraid of the dark.
She tiptoed across the kitchen floor, quiet as a mouse.
"Hooray!" shouted the children, clapping their hands.
The rain went pitter-patter on the old tin roof.
Do you remember what happened to the brave little boat?
Far, far away, across the deep blue sea, there was an island made of candy.
The bear yawned a great big yawn and rubbed his eyes.
"Please wait for me!" called the littlest duck.
Grandma's soup was warm and smelled of carrots and thyme.
One, two, three, four, five little frogs sat on a log.
The wind howled, and the trees bent low.
"I can do it all by myself," said the little girl proudly.
Shh. Can you hear the owl hooting in the forest?
The fox looked left, then right, then left again.
What do you think the giant will say?
The train rumbled over the bridge, chugga-chugga, choo-choo!
They shared their berries, and nobody was hungry anymore.
"Thank you," said the mouse. "You are a true friend."
The snow fell softly, covering the garden in white.
Every morning, the rooster crowed, cock-a-doodle-doo!
The little turtle walked slowly, but he never gave up.
"Oh no, my balloon!" cried the boy, as it floated up into the sky.
Inside the box was a tiny golden key.
The stars twinkled like diamonds above the quiet sea.
Can you find the hidden butterfly in the picture?
"Let's build a castle out of pillows," said Mom.
The puppy wagged his tail so hard that he almost fell over.
Deep in the jungle, a parrot sang a cheerful song.
The princess climbed the tallest tower to see the sunrise.
"Are we there yet?" asked the twins for the hundredth time.
The old clock struck twelve, bong, bong, bong.
A little seed slept under the ground, waiting for spring.
"Don't worry," said Dad. "I'll always come back for you."
The elephant sprayed water high into the air, whoosh!
Why do you think the moon follows our car at night?
The baker's bread was golden, crusty, and still warm.
"Sorry," said the bunny. "I didn't mean to step on your tail."
The kite danced in the wind, higher and higher.
Under the bridge lived a grumpy troll who loved riddles.
She opened the window, and the smell of flowers filled the room.
"Ready, set, go!" The race had begun.
The little lamb followed Mary everywhere she went.
Bubbles floated through the bathroom, pop, pop, pop!
How many apples can you count on the tree?
The pirate's ship had red sails and a very noisy parrot.
"I love you to the moon and back," whispered Mama.
The caterpillar ate and ate, and then he fell asleep.
When he woke up, he had become a beautiful butterfly.
Thunder rumbled, but they were safe and dry inside.
"Look!" said Sam. "A rainbow!"
The penguins slid down the ice, one after another.
Where would you go if you could fly?
The little robot beeped twice and blinked its blue eyes.
Together, the friends carried the heavy basket up the hill.
"Hmm," said the owl, "that is a very good question."
And they all lived happily ever after.
The end. Sweet dreams, my love.
